hypotheses_validated.claim: Verifier MAJOR (round 2): both pull_request_target gates followed links in the pull request, so a PR that turns tests/ (or governance/) into an absolute link to $WS/base/... passed without a label. Real, and fixed
hypotheses_validated.evidence: Reproduced first with the verifier's own scripts in WSL (scratchpad h05g2/symlink_attack.sh, symlink_decisions.sh): golden.yml command rc=0 'golden lock matches the base revision', ci.yml lock rc=0 and --run 'golden suite OK: 1 passed' on the stub; decisions.yml command 'decision breaker OK: 0 of 8 ... retired' rc=0 vs 'CIRCUIT BREAKER: 8 of 8' for the same content as plain files. Fixes: (1) check_golden.py --rev REV reads the change only from git objects (ls-tree -r -t -z of the commit, cat-file blob); a 120000/160000 entry at tests, tests/golden or below is a LINK, a file at tests means no golden suite; links fail even with --acknowledged; --rev refuses --run/--update and a --root that is not the top level of a checkout (rev-parse --show-cdup). (2) The working-tree check refuses a link at tests/ or tests/golden/ and never reads the lock through one; --update refuses to lock through links. (3) adr.py read_rev (git objects) and read_checkout (working tree) raise RecordError for a link/submodule/non-file at governance/, governance/decisions/, an ADR-*.md or INVARIANTS.md, and for non-UTF-8 records: exit 1 for lint, index and breaker, also with --acknowledged and on the base side. (4) golden.yml/decisions.yml run 'check_golden.py --root pr --rev HEAD ...' and 'adr.py breaker --root pr --rev HEAD --base-root base'. After the fix the same adapted WSL scripts (PR side as a git checkout, real symlinks): golden.yml gate rc=1 'LINK tests' without and with the label; ci.yml lock and --run rc=1 'LINK tests'; decisions.yml rc=1 'governance is not a directory at HEAD (mode 120000)' without and with the label; working tree rc=1. Tests: test_golden_gate_never_follows_a_linked_tests_directory (both workflows' layouts, workflow commands extracted from the YAML, link made by git on POSIX or as a junction on Windows, the link is shown to resolve before it is refused), test_golden_rev_reads_git_objects_only (links and submodules at tests, tests/golden, below, and the manifest; file at tests; committed unchecked .pyc; working tree ignored), test_golden_lock_rejects_links (tests/ link case, --update refusal), test_decisions_gate_as_the_workflow_runs_it (governance/ link case), test_adr_records_behind_links_or_not_files_are_refused, test_adr_read_rev_takes_only_plain_files.

hypotheses_validated.claim: Verifier minor: the gates checked out the mutable refs/pull/N/merge without checking it belongs to the event's head. Real (design level); fixed with merge_ref.py, run before each gate
hypotheses_validated.evidence: New governance/tools/merge_ref.py: the merge commit (HEAD of pr) must have exactly two parents, the second equal to --head (github.event.pull_request.head.sha, passed via env) and the first equal to the base checkout's commit or an ancestor of it (git merge-base --is-ancestor in the base checkout, which golden.yml/decisions.yml now fetch with fetch-depth: 0). Parents are read from the raw commit object (cat-file commit, header only), because in the depth-1 checkout actions/checkout makes 'rev-parse HEAD^2' fails (asserted in the test). Parent ids are validated as object ids before use as git arguments. test_merge_ref_must_be_this_events_head_merged_into_the_base with temporary repos (shallow merge checkout): OK for base b1 and for a newer base b2 ('an ancestor of base'); stale head rc 1; merge into a newer base than the lock's rc 1; shallow base rc 1 'unknown to the base checkout ... fetch-depth: 0'; 1-, 3- and 0-parent commits rc 1; message lines 'parent X' ignored; bad arguments rc 2; and the workflow step command itself in the workflow layout. A race on GitHub itself was not reproduced (no GitHub).

hypotheses_validated.claim: Verifier minor: the ADR breaker let a decided ADR be rewritten via demotion to Proposed, free text on the Status line or text before the first section. Real, and fixed
hypotheses_validated.evidence: The verifier's adr_probe.py before: step 1 (Accepted->Proposed) rc 0, step 2 rc 0, preamble note rc 0. After: step 1 rc 1 'moved back', preamble rc 1. adr.parse now keeps a frozen text: the whole file, whitespace-collapsed, with only the status word, a YYYY-MM-DD Date value and well-formed Superseded-by ids masked (free text on those lines stays; field-like lines inside sections are body text). Status changes allowed: unchanged, Accepted->Deprecated, Accepted->Superseded, Deprecated->Superseded (adr.RETIREMENTS); anything else trips. Lint: Status must be exactly one word; Supersedes/Superseded-by entries must be ADR-NNNN or [ADR-NNNN](ADR-NNNN-slug.md) with matching ids. Records read as bytes are CRLF-normalised (as the old text-mode readers did). Tests: test_adr_breaker_freezes_decided_records_except_retirement (10 rewrite forms trip, 5 retirement forms do not, full status-transition table, notes on a base Status line, field-like line in a section), test_adr_lint_takes_exact_status_and_successor_forms.

hypotheses_validated.claim: Verifier minor: unusable schemas crashed or failed per file under jsonschema/auto, and the engines disagreed. Real, and fixed; two further disagreements found and fixed
hypotheses_validated.evidence: The verifier's schema_probe2.py before: tracebacks for null and $schema 5, per-file PointerToNowhere/Unresolvable/MemoryError, root true rc 0 vs 2, duplicate required/type, title 5, $id 5 rc 0 vs 2. After: every case exits 2 under both engines with the same verdict (rc 1 cases enum [] and property false stay rc 1 under both). Changes: precheck_schema for both engines (JSON object; $schema absent or draft 2020-12/2019-09; $id only at the root; every $ref a local JSON pointer resolving to a subschema reached structurally, percent-decoding and array indices supported; no $dynamicRef/$recursiveRef; no patternProperties, whose keys jsonschema matches with Python's re; every pattern translatable); jsonschema_check_schema maps any jsonschema exception to SchemaError and no longer asserts formats on the metaschema check; MiniValidator checks unique type/required arrays and the types of $schema, $id, $comment, title, description, deprecated, readOnly, writeOnly, examples; the ECMA translator rejects a repeat count above 65535 and nested minimum counts whose product exceeds 65535 ((?:){2147483648} took 108.7 s then MemoryError when probed). Found while fixing: jsonschema asserted every format it knows while the built-in engine asserted only date-time (old jsonschema checker: 1 error each for email, ipv4, uri, hostname, regex, date on 'T05-governance(', built-in 0); now both assert only date-time. Tests: test_handover_engines_agree_on_unusable_schemas (26 cases x builtin/auto/jsonschema), test_handover_schema_precheck_and_references, test_handover_engines_assert_the_same_formats, test_ecma_repeat_bounds.

hypotheses_falsified.claim: The gate can read the merge commit's parents with 'git rev-parse HEAD^2' in the checkout actions/checkout makes
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: In a depth-1 clone (as actions/checkout fetches a ref) the shallow commit's parents are grafted away: rev-parse HEAD^2 fails and %P is empty, while 'git cat-file commit HEAD' still shows both parent lines (scratch probe, then asserted in the merge_ref test). merge_ref.py reads the raw commit object.

hypotheses_falsified.claim: jsonschema's metaschema check and instance validation are engine-independent once 'regex' is left out
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: Format assertions depend on installed optional packages (uri, hostname here) and asserted formats the built-in engine ignores (6 of 6 probed). Format assertion was removed from the metaschema check and limited to date-time for instances.

hypotheses_falsified.claim: A malformed parent line in a merge commit could reach 'git merge-base' as an option
hypotheses_falsified.evidence: An object written with 'git hash-object -t commit --literally' and 'parent --output=x' is refused by 'git rev-parse --verify <oid>^{commit}' (git 2.4x, Windows), so it never gets that far; merge_ref.parents validates parent ids anyway (tested in-process).
